theme: Airbnb corporate footprint signals: careers/Greenhouse job-posting scrapers, LinkedIn headcount trackers, layoffs.fyi data, Glassdoor/Indeed review datasets, GitHub org activity (GH Archive)
queries_run: github repo layoffs.fyi dataset csv scraper (blocked by exhausted WebSearch budget, fallback to WebFetch)
github greenhouse job board api scraper python company job postings dataset (blocked)
github GH Archive company org activity dataset commits (blocked)
github glassdoor reviews dataset scraper company (blocked)
WebFetch duckduckgo html search x2 (captcha blocked)
WebFetch bing.com/search x2 (returned generic github.com pages, useless)
notes: Session-wide WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200 used by other scouts) before this scout ran any query, so all discovery had to go through WebFetch instead: (1) github.com/search?q=... pages return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (Retry-After 3600) — search endpoint is rate-limited across the whole run, other scouts should expect the same; (2) DuckDuckGo HTML search returns a CAPTCHA page to fetchers; (3) Bing via WebFetch renders only the generic github.com/login/signup boilerplate, not real SERP content (likely JS-rendered results the fetcher's markdown conversion drops) — Bing is not a usable WebSearch substitute via WebFetch. Working substitute: github.com/topics/<tag> pages fetch fine and list real repos with descriptions; individual github.com/<owner>/<repo> pages also fetch fine. Recommend future scouts hitting the WebSearch cap route through github.com/topics/* and direct repo URLs rather than github.com/search. Best finds this theme: APVentureEngine/warn-act-notices (comprehensive normalized WARN Act archive, 61k+ notices, 48 states, daily-updated) and kadoa-org/layoffs-tracker (42k notices, different normalization/source pipeline) both plausibly contain Airbnb's 2020 mass-layoff WARN filings (California) and any subsequent smaller ones — worth a direct company-name grep once pulled, since Airbnb headcount cuts are a real corporate-footprint event. Did not verify Airbnb appears by name in any of these (no data was downloaded/queried, per rules — cataloguing only). LinkedIn 'headcount over time' specifically does not appear to exist as an open GitHub dataset; all LinkedIn scrapers are live-scrape tools (current snapshot only, ToS-risk, left as method/do-not-run). No dedicated Airbnb-specific Glassdoor/Greenhouse repo found. Airbnb's own GitHub org (github.com/airbnb, 204 public repos, active as of Sep 2026) is real engineering-output signal but is a company page, not a third-party catalogued dataset — flagged as a pointer/context row only; OpenDigger (X-lab2017) is the actual tool that would let someone turn that + GH Archive into a time series (contributor/commit counts by month) for airbnb's public repos as an engineering-investment/headcount-adjacent proxy.

candidates.name: warn-act-notices
candidates.what_it_holds: Normalized US WARN Act mass-layoff/plant-closure notice archive, 1988-present, 61,309+ records as of 13 Sep 2026, covering 48 states (excludes AR, NH, WY which don't publish company-level notices). CSV and JSON, per-state files under data/by-state/, plus monthly/yearly time-series, employer rollups, RSS/ics calendar exports. Fields: employer name, canonical normalized employer name, location, employees affected, notice date, effective date, notice type (layoff/closure), state. Auto-updated daily (15 consecutive daily commits Aug30-Sep13 2026 observed). Built on Apache-2.0 biglocalnews/warn-scraper (Stanford Big Local News) as the underlying collector; this repo's own data is CC BY 4.0.
candidates.why_useful: Direct, company-name-searchable, point-in-time-stamped (daily commits) layoff-notice history that should contain Airbnb's California WARN filings from the 2020 mass layoff (~1,900 employees) and any later reductions — a real, dated headcount-shock signal (gap #14, corporate footprint) rather than a scraped estimate. Also usable as a macro/consumer-labor-market cross-check independent of ABNB.
candidates.license: CC BY 4.0 (data), Apache-2.0 (underlying scraper it builds on)

candidates.name: layoffs-tracker (kadoa)
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source dataset + interactive dashboard (Vite/React/sql.js) of ~42,000 mass-layoff and plant-closure notices aggregated from 45 state labor departments, normalized via kadoa.com's parsing pipeline. Ships a lazily-loaded full SQLite database plus a JSON summary file for the overview. MIT licensed, 137 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A second, independently-sourced/normalized WARN-notice dataset (different coverage/parsing than APVentureEngine's) — cross-checking two independent WARN aggregations reduces normalization risk before trusting any Airbnb-specific layoff date/count pulled from either.
candidates.time_coverage: not stated precisely; WARN-era coverage, recent

candidates.name: layoffs-tracker (evgeniimatveev, layoffs.fyi mirror)
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive dashboard mirroring the layoffs.fyi-via-Kaggle tech-layoffs dataset: 2,412 layoff events across 1,713 companies in 49 countries, 2020-2025, ingested into a committed DuckDB file (layoffs.duckdb) via ingest.py. KPI cards, timeline, industry breakdown, company rankings, funding-stage cuts, choropleth map. 34 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, queryable (DuckDB) mirror of the canonical layoffs.fyi tech-layoffs tracker — the actual source most 'layoffs data' searches point back to. Should contain Airbnb's 2020 layoff event (company, date, count, % of workforce) as one row, giving a directly comparable cross-company layoff-severity metric.

candidates.name: glassdoor-review-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python + Selenium/Chromedriver scraper that logs into Glassdoor and exports a target company's employee reviews (ratings, text, dates) to CSV, with date-range filtering; ~1.5s/review throughput. BSD-2-Clause, 23 commits. README explicitly notes Glassdoor's ToS prohibits scraping and accounts risk bans.
candidates.why_useful: A working, well-known method for pulling Airbnb's own Glassdoor review history (rating trend, review volume, text) as an employee-sentiment / attrition-risk proxy that correlates with headcount and culture stress — but requires login credentials and violates Glassdoor ToS, so per repo rules this is catalogued as method only and NOT to be run without a human ToS decision.

candidates.name: JobSpy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python job-scraping library aggregating listings concurrently from LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, Google, ZipRecruiter, Bayt, Naukri, Bdjobs. Returns title, company, location (country/city/state), remote status, description, employment type, salary min/max/currency, posting date, plus site-specific fields (e.g. LinkedIn job level). MIT, 4.3k stars, 842 forks, 353 commits. No documented direct company-name filter parameter, but company field is returned so results can be filtered client-side.
candidates.why_useful: One tool that could pull Airbnb's live open-roles count/mix across five+ job boards simultaneously as a hiring-pace / headcount-growth proxy (careers/Greenhouse angle) — more general and more actively maintained than a single-ATS Greenhouse scraper. Method only; not run.
candidates.time_coverage: n/a — live snapshot only, no historical archive
candidates.last_activity: not stated (353 commits, 4.3k stars — actively used project)

candidates.name: gharchive.org
candidates.what_it_holds: Source code for the GH Archive project itself (gharchive.org): crawling scripts, BigQuery integration/queries, and site content that together record and make queryable all public GitHub events (pushes, PRs, issues, stars, etc.) since 2011. MIT (code), CC-BY-4.0 (site content). 3.1k stars, 230 forks, 30 open issues, 146 commits. The event archive/data itself is hosted externally (BigQuery public dataset, gharchive.org hourly JSON.gz files), not committed to this repo.
candidates.why_useful: The canonical entry point for pulling Airbnb's own public-GitHub-org activity (commit/PR/star velocity across its 200+ public repos) as an engineering-investment / indirect headcount-growth proxy — gap #15. Method/pointer, not a committed dataset in the repo itself.
candidates.size_hint: external: full GH event archive (BigQuery / gharchive.org gz files), TBs

candidates.name: OpenDigger
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source analytics platform (X-lab) that processes GH Archive data into precomputed per-repo/per-org monthly metrics (OpenRank, commit counts, contributor counts, star/fork trends, activity indices), served as JSON files plus sample data directories and Jupyter notebooks; TS/Node primary implementation with Python variants. Apache-2.0, 1,083 commits, 17 open issues, 4 open PRs, actively developed.
candidates.why_useful: Directly usable to build a monthly time series of Airbnb's public-GitHub-org engineering activity (its ~200 public repos) without writing GH Archive/BigQuery queries from scratch — a ready-made input for the 'own GitHub org activity' engagement gap (#15) and, as an aside, a template for scoring any competitor's or partner's OSS output.

candidates.name: py-linkedin-jobs-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/headless-browser library scraping public LinkedIn job listings: job id, title, company, location, links, salary/benefits, easy-apply flag, applicant counts, employment type and experience-level filters, geoId-based geographic filtering, adaptive rate limiting, session persistence, CLI + programmatic API, JSON/CSV/table output. MIT, 189 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Could be pointed at Airbnb's LinkedIn job listings to build an open-roles count and mix (function, seniority, geography) over time as a hiring-pace/headcount-growth proxy — same use case as JobSpy but LinkedIn-specific with richer per-posting metadata (applicant counts). Method only, current-snapshot, ToS caveats apply; not run.

candidates.name: Airbnb GitHub organization
candidates.what_it_holds: Airbnb's own public GitHub org: 204 public repositories, 5.7k org followers, verified, San Francisco. Actively updated flagship repos as of Sep 2026 include chronon (Scala ML data platform, 1,048 stars, updated 11 Sep 2026), HorizonCalendar (Swift, 3,158 stars, updated 3 Sep 2026), viaduct (Kotlin GraphQL, 173 stars, updated 12 Sep 2026), plus long-running high-star projects (javascript style guide 148k stars, lottie-android/ios ~26-36k stars). Not itself a downloadable dataset — a live org page.
candidates.why_useful: Raw source that OpenDigger / GH Archive tooling would point at to build the 'own GitHub org activity' engagement time series (gap #15); repo-update cadence and new-repo creation rate are a free, real-time proxy for engineering headcount and investment focus (e.g. chronon/viaduct being actively pushed suggests current data-platform and GraphQL infra investment).
